slides.body: Five mistakes to watch for.

items: Expecting a cherry-picked commit to have the original's ID. Root cause: the commit ID is computed from the tree and the parent as well; the same change on another parent is another snapshot and another commit.
Reading only git diff and missing what is staged. Root cause: it compares the index with the working tree; git diff --cached compares HEAD with the index, and git diff HEAD covers the whole distance.
Counting on the reflog to recover something on the server or in another clone. Root cause: reflogs are local and are not shared with remotes; bare repositories keep none by default.

Believing that a staged secret never left a trace because it was never committed. Root cause: git add stores content at once; the blob is an object in .git/objects until garbage collection removes it.
Treating origin/main as the branch on the server. Root cause: a remote-tracking branch records the last-known state of the remote branch, as of the last fetch.

beats.text: If a commit is a diff, a list of changed lines, they're the same thing and should have the same ID. They don't. If a commit is a snapshot, a full picture of the project, they're different things. But they have the same message, the same author date, and they change the same line. So which is it? Say it out loud.

beats.text: The three trees. In one sentence: a file can exist in three states at the same time, in the commit that HEAD names, in the index and in the working tree, and git status reports the differences between them.
beats.tele: The three trees. In one sentence: a file can exist in three states at the same time, in the commit that HEAD names, in the index and in the working tree, and `git status` reports the differences between them.

beats.text: Now precisely. "Tree" here means a complete set of files, not a tree object. The commit that HEAD names is the last snapshot, and HEAD is the name for where you are now. The index is the proposed next snapshot: every tracked path with the ID of a blob, one file's content. The working tree is the files on disk. git add copies content from the working tree into the index, and git commit turns the index into tree objects and a commit.
beats.tele: Now precisely. "Tree" here means a complete set of files, not a tree object. The commit that HEAD names is the last snapshot, and HEAD is the name for where you are now. The index is the proposed next snapshot: every tracked path with the ID of a blob, one file's content. The working tree is the files on disk. `git add` copies content from the working tree into the index, and `git commit` turns the index into tree objects and a commit.

beats.text: Two commands compare neighbouring pairs. git diff --cached compares HEAD with the index. git diff compares the index with the working tree. Neither shows the whole distance from HEAD to the working tree. git diff HEAD does.
beats.tele: Two commands compare neighbouring pairs. `git diff --cached` compares HEAD with the index. `git diff` compares the index with the working tree. Neither shows the whole distance from HEAD to the working tree. `git diff HEAD` does.

beats.text: Two views of a commit. "A commit is a diff" is wrong as a statement about storage, and right as a way to read history. You need both views, and you need to know which one a command uses.
beats.tele: Two views of a commit. "A commit is a diff" is wrong as a statement about storage, and right as a way to read history. You need both views, and you need to know which one a command uses.

beats.text: The snapshot view: the tree that the commit records. It is used by checkout, by builds, by git ls-tree, by git diff A B, and by merge, which works on three snapshots.
beats.tele: The snapshot view: the tree that the commit records. It is used by checkout, by builds, by `git ls-tree`, by `git diff A B`, and by merge, which works on three snapshots.

beats.text: The change view: the difference between the commit's tree and its parent's, computed on demand. It is used by git show, by git log -p, by cherry-pick, by rebase and by revert.
beats.tele: The change view: the difference between the commit's tree and its parent's, computed on demand. It is used by `git show`, by `git log -p`, by cherry-pick, by rebase and by revert.

beats.text: Take cherry-pick as the test case, with the two branches from the hook on screen. Cherry-pick copies one commit's change onto another branch. The manual describes it in the change view: it applies the change that a commit introduces and records a new commit. The implementation is a three-way merge whose base is the parent of the picked commit, so it works on three snapshots.
beats.tele: Take cherry-pick as the test case, with the two branches from the hook on screen. Cherry-pick copies one commit's change onto another branch. The manual describes it in the change view: it applies the change that a commit introduces and records a new commit. The implementation is a three-way merge whose base is the parent of the picked commit, so it works on three snapshots.

beats.text: Rebase repeats this for a series of commits, and revert applies the inverse change. The result is always a new commit with a new ID. git cherry-pick carries the label 🟡 CAUTION: it adds one commit to the current branch, which moves it, and updates the index and the working tree.

beats.text: The wrong models. The textbook's table has eleven rows. Here are the four this video proves, each with its reality.
beats.tele: The wrong models. The textbook's table has eleven rows. Here are the four this video proves, each with its reality.

beats.text: Wrong: a commit stores a diff. Reality: a commit records a full snapshot, the ID of the top-level tree, with its parents, author, committer and message. Diffs are computed on demand. You saw the proof in video 7.
beats.tele: Wrong: a commit stores a diff. Reality: a commit records a full snapshot, the ID of the top-level tree, with its parents, author, committer and message. Diffs are computed on demand. You saw the proof in video 7.

beats.text: Wrong: a branch is a copy of the code, with a parent branch. Reality: a branch is a ref that names one commit, and Git has no notion of a parent branch. You saw the proof in video 9: creating a branch added no object.
beats.tele: Wrong: a branch is a copy of the code, with a parent branch. Reality: a branch is a ref that names one commit, and Git has no notion of a parent branch. You saw the proof in video 9: creating a branch added no object.

beats.text: Wrong: a commit belongs to a branch. Reality: "the commits on a branch" is the set reachable from the commit the branch names. One commit can be reachable from many refs or from none. You saw both in video 9.
beats.tele: Wrong: a commit belongs to a branch. Reality: "the commits on a branch" is the set reachable from the commit the branch names. One commit can be reachable from many refs or from none. You saw both in video 9.

beats.text: Five mistakes to watch for.
beats.tele: Five mistakes to watch for.

beats.text: Expecting a cherry-picked commit to have the original's ID. Root cause: the commit ID is computed from the tree and the parent as well; the same change on another parent is another snapshot and another commit.
beats.tele: Expecting a cherry-picked commit to have the original's ID. Root cause: the commit ID is computed from the tree and the parent as well; the same change on another parent is another snapshot and another commit.

beats.text: Reading only git diff and missing what is staged. Root cause: it compares the index with the working tree; git diff --cached compares HEAD with the index, and git diff HEAD covers the whole distance.
beats.tele: Reading only `git diff` and missing what is staged. Root cause: it compares the index with the working tree; `git diff --cached` compares HEAD with the index, and `git diff HEAD` covers the whole distance.

beats.text: Counting on the reflog to recover something on the server or in another clone. Root cause: reflogs are local and are not shared with remotes; bare repositories keep none by default.
beats.tele: Counting on the reflog to recover something on the server or in another clone. Root cause: reflogs are local and are not shared with remotes; bare repositories keep none by default.

beats.text: Believing that a staged secret never left a trace because it was never committed. Root cause: git add stores content at once; the blob is an object in .git/objects until garbage collection removes it.
beats.tele: Believing that a staged secret never left a trace because it was never committed. Root cause: `git add` stores content at once; the blob is an object in `.git/objects` until garbage collection removes it.

beats.text: Treating origin/main as the branch on the server. Root cause: a remote-tracking branch records the last-known state of the remote branch, as of the last fetch.
beats.tele: Treating `origin/main` as the branch on the server. Root cause: a remote-tracking branch records the last-known state of the remote branch, as of the last fetch.

beats.text: Now, out of the lab. An inference team maintains a release branch that must not receive a capacity change made on main. A fix to the client's retry count lands on main after that capacity change. The team cherry-picks the fix. The change view tells them what the cherry-pick will carry over: one line in client.yaml.
beats.tele: Now, out of the lab. An inference team maintains a release branch that must not receive a capacity change made on `main`. A fix to the client's retry count lands on `main` after that capacity change. The team cherry-picks the fix. The change view tells them what the cherry-pick will carry over: one line in `client.yaml`.

beats.text: The snapshot view tells them what the release build will contain afterwards: the retry fix, and still two workers. An engineer who holds only the diff model can't explain why the two commits have different IDs. One who holds only the snapshot model fears that the release now contains everything main has.

beats.text: A commit is stored as a snapshot and can be read as a change against its parent. Checkout, builds and merge use the snapshot, and show, cherry-pick, rebase and revert use the change. A cherry-pick makes a new commit with the same change and a different snapshot.
